comments.story_title: The Witness: the creator of Braid talks about his fiendishly difficult new game
comments.why_zh: 关于 Jai 的系列视频改变了人对编程的看法。
comments.quote_zh: 看这些视频极大地改变了我对编程的思考方式。
comments.text_zh: 我强烈建议任何对编程语言感兴趣的人去看他关于 Jai 的系列视频，那是他为自己下一款游戏创造的语言。从这里开始：[VIDEO] 它还没发布，但看这些视频极大地改变了我对编程的思考方式。"数据驱动编程"这个概念——我会把它描述为"只搬动你不得不搬动的数据"——对我来说真是醍醐灌顶。我算是从 Ruby 世界出来的（再之前是 Java），那里的态度更像是"把一切都抽象掉！"我一直在试着把 Blow 的许多原则应用到我的 JavaScript 编程中，效果非常棒。我发现自己更贴近"底层"了（在 JavaScript 世界里就是纯 Node 和底层浏览器 API），而且收获巨大。我也很欣赏他实用主义优先于理想主义的方针。比如我觉得 React 世界把一个好想法（不可变性可以理清数据流）变成了一种宗教（一切都必须不可变！）。看 Blow 工作给了我底气去避开那一套。就像学 Rails 让我成为更好的程序员一样（尽管我已经不用它了，也否定了它的很多前提），我发现学 Jai 确实让我作为程序员和计算机科学思考者的水平提升了一个档次。
comments.text: I strongly encourage anyone interested in programming languages to watch his series about Jai, the language he is creating for his next game. Starts here: [VIDEO] It's not released yet, but watching the videos has massively changed the way I think about programming. The notion of "data-driven programming," which I would describe as "only move around the data you have to", has been a real revelation to me. I sort of came out of the Ruby world (and Java before that) where the attitude is more "Abstract all the things!" I have been trying to apply many of Blow's principles in my JavaScript programming and it has been awesome. I find myself staying closer to the "metal" (which in JavaScript world is pure Node and low-level browser APIs) and it has been incredibly rewarding. I've also really enjoyed his policy of pragmatism over idealism. I think the React world for example has taken a good idea (immutability can clarify data flows) and turned it into a religion (Everything Must Be Immutable!) Watching Blow work has given me the confidence to steer away from that. Much in the same way that learning Rails made me a better programmer (even though I don't use it anymore, and I've rejected a lot of its premises) I have found learning Jai has really leveled me up as a programmer and a computer science thinker.

comments.why_zh: 这一系列视频中的数据驱动理念适用于任何编程底层载体。
comments.quote_zh: 彻底改变了我写代码的方式
comments.text_zh: 这有点像个无底洞，但 Jonathan Blow 的“Ideas for a programming language about games”以及随后的一系列视频彻底改变了我写代码的方式：[VIDEO] 讽刺的是，我是个 JavaScript 程序员，而 Blow 讨厌 JavaScript，他认为这跟他的编码风格完全相悖。但说实话，我觉得这些想法非常通用：他提出的是我心目中的“数据驱动编程”，用我的话说就是“只动那些你不得不动的比特”。而这个核心想法可以映射到任何底层载体上。Blow 对以处理器指令之外的东西为目标感到反感，Jai（他的新语言）就是沿着这个思路发展的。但我完全可以把同样的想法用到 V8 上……你其实可以用任何底层载体……我也可以面向 Minecraft 方块，用同样的方式写代码。这只需要退后一步，问一句：要让那个底层载体到达它该在的位置，最少需要多少次写入。然后，与其写 Rails 或 Webpack 那种庞然大物般的声明式编程结构，你只需写出让那些比特翻转所需的最少函数调用，别的什么都不做。Blow 基于这些概念写了一门全新的语言和编译器，但我发现这些想法可以移植到任何任意的 API 目标上。
comments.text: It’s a bit of a rabbit hole, but Jonathan Blow’s “Ideas for a programming language about games” and all the subsequent videos have totally revolutionized how I code: [VIDEO] The irony of it is I’m a JavaScript programmer and Blow hates JavaScript, he thinks it’s antithetical to his style of coding. But really, I think the ideas are very generic: he proposes what I think of as “data-driven programming” which in my head means “only move the bits you have to.” And that core idea maps to any substrate. Blow is offended by the idea of targeting something other than processor instructions, and Jai (his new language) develops along those lines. But I have no problem applying the same ideas to V8... you can really use any substrate... I could target Minecraft blocks and code in the same way. It just requires stepping back and asking what the minimum number of writes needed to get that substrate where it needs to be. And then rather than writing some monstrous declarative programming structure like Rails or Webpack, you just write the minimal function calls needed to make those bits flip and thing more. Blow writes a whole new language and compiler based on those concepts, but I find the ideas translate to any arbitrary API target.

comments.author: erikpukinskis
comments.story_title: Jonathan Blow: “C++ is a weird mess”
comments.why_zh: 对 Jai 的密集介绍，也是观看发明一门语言过程的启发。
comments.quote_zh: 我还发现，作为一个程序员，看他发明这门语言的过程极有启发性。
comments.text_zh: 我有点失望他没公开源码，但我也理解。他希望在设计语言的过程中能自由地对语言做重大改动，而如果别人已经在用了，这就更难了。话虽如此，如果你想知道 Jai 是关于什么的，我建议从他的第一个视频看起：[VIDEO] 最开始的几十个视频都相当密集，他相当高效地讲了这门语言的基础。（他最近的视频更像是开发日志）是的，看视频很慢，但对我来说，如果没有这些背景，我大概不会领会他的设计选择。我还发现，作为一个程序员，看他发明这门语言的过程极有启发性。过去几年里，它实质性地塑造了我自己的流程和思考方式。
comments.text: I am a little disappointed he hasn’t released the source, but I am also sympathetic. He wants to be free to change major things about the language while he’s designing it, and that’s harder if other people are using it. That said, if you want to know what Jai is about, I recommend starting from his first video: [VIDEO] The first couple dozen videos are all pretty dense, with him presenting the basics of the language pretty efficiently. (His more recent vids are more like development vlogs) Yes, videos are slow, but for me I don’t think I would’ve appreciated his design choices without all the context. I also found watching his process for inventing the language extremely instructive, just as a programmer. It has substantially formed my own process and thinking over the last few years.

comments.why_zh: 主张设计一种既高性能又编程有趣的语言。
comments.quote_zh: 我们应该设计一种既高性能又编程有趣的语言。
comments.text_zh: 这里有人看过 Jonathan Blow 关于他的语言想法的视频吗？[VIDEO] 我不关心他语言的具体细节，但我认为他提出了一个非常有道理的观点，我的总结是：我们应该设计一种既高性能又编程起来有趣的语言。有趣 = 少写样板代码，让重构更容易。C++ 不是那种语言，而从我看过的内容来看，Rust 也不是那种语言。C++ 被向后兼容性困住了，所以可以说它永远无法实现那些目标。Rust 似乎没有把这些当作目标，它有其他目标，所以它也不是一门有趣的语言。太啰嗦了，至少我读到的是这样。
comments.text: As anyone here watched the Jonathan Blow videos on his language ideas? [VIDEO] I don't care about the specifics of his language but I think he brings up a very valid point which my summary would be, we should design a language that is both performant AND fun to program. Fun = type less boilerplate, make refactoring easier. C++ is not that language and from what I've read Rust is not that language either. C++ is stuck with backward compatibility so it can arguably never achieve those goals. Rust didn't seem to have those goals it mind, it had other goals so it's not really a fun language either. Too verbose or so I've read.

comments.why_zh: 从游戏行业视角看取代 C++，与 Rust 推动内存安全的方向不同。
comments.quote_zh: 对在游戏行业语境下演进 C++（更确切地说，是造一门新语言来取代它）有很多想法
comments.text_zh: Jonathan Blow（cult/独立游戏开发者/工作室老板）对于在游戏行业语境下演进 C++（更确切地说，是造一门新语言来取代它）有很多想法。这个视角很有意思，因为它某种程度上是从另一个角度出发的，偏离了 Rust 正在做的“内存安全、更强保证”这一项目。[VIDEO] 就像从 90 年代开始，脚本语言从 C/C++ 的使用中咬下了一大块，我认为我们现在正看到 C/C++ 的另外几个用例被抢走：1）对性能敏感但也对安全敏感的东西（Rust）；2）对性能超级敏感，以至于 Rust 和 C++ 实际上都太臃肿，但它又并不是真的对安全敏感，所以 Rust/现代 C++ 提供的那些保证并不值得（Jai，Blow 的语言）。第 1 类显然真实存在，但第 2 类可能太小，难以自我维持（尽管 Blow 从经济角度论证过它值得做）。我们是不是就一直用更专门好用的语言从 C/C++ 用户群里一层层剥人，直到最后只剩下维护遗留代码的人？还是说在某些用例里 C++ 仍然会继续合理？我猜这在很大程度上取决于我们能否通过标准流程有意义地“现代化”C++，而不是仅仅再拧上一大堆增加臃肿的特性。我不太敢押注这个把戏能成功。
comments.text: Jonathan Blow (cult/indie game developer/studio owner) has a lot of ideas about evolving C++ (or rather, building a new language to replace it) specifically in a game industry context. This perspective is interesting because its kind of running at a different angle away from the "memory-safe, better guarantees" project that Rust is workin on. [VIDEO] Just as the scripting languages took a big bite out of C/C++ usage starting in the 90s, I think we're seeing another couple use-case for C/C++ pull off: 1) stuff that is performance sensitive but security sensitive as well (Rust) 2) stuff that is soooo performance sensitive that Rust and C++ are actually too bloated, but which isn't really security sensitive so the guarantees that Rust/Modern C++ offer aren't worth it (Jai, Blow's language). Category 1 is clearly real, but Category 2 might be too small to sustain itself (though Blow makes an economic argument that it would be worth it). Are we just going to keep peeling back C/C++ users from the pack with more specifically-useful languages until there are none left except for those maintaining legacy code? Or are there use-cases where C++ will continue to make sense? I guess a lot of this depends on whether or not we can meaningfully "modernize" C++ through the standards process without simply bolting on a lot more features that add to the bloat. I wouldn't wager much that this trick can be pulled off.

comments.quote_zh: 认为性能与专注于你试图解决的问题密切相关
comments.text_zh: 这在精神上非常接近 Casey Muratori（Handmade Hero）的“Compression Oriented Programming”[LINK]。对于那些同时抱怨（缺少）泛型和高性能系统级编程的人来说，这一点以及他在电子游戏行业的同道——比如 Mike Acton（Data Oriented Design in C++）[LINK] 和 Jonathan Blow（Ideas about a new programming language for games）[VIDEO]——都认为，性能与专注于你试图解决的问题密切相关。不必要的抽象层级（尤其是那些违背硬件的抽象），以及泛泛地试图解决你永远不会实际用到的情形，都是在浪费真实的性能和开发者的时间。
comments.text: This is very much in spirit to Casey Muratori's (Handmade Hero) 'Compression Oriented Programming' [LINK] For all the people complaining about both (the lack of) generics and high performance systems level programming, this and his allies in the video game industry such as Mike Acton (Data Oriented Design in C++) [LINK] and Jonathan Blow (Ideas about a new programming language for games) [VIDEO] argue that performance and the focusing on the problem you are trying to solve are intimately related. Needless levels of abstraction (particularly ones that go against the hardware) and generically trying to solve for cases you will never actually use is a waste of real performance and developer time.

comments.author: jstimpfle
comments.story_title: Non-determinism: a sublanguage rather than a monad
comments.why_zh: Blow 的“Big Agenda language”批评：意识形态纯粹的语言可用性更差。
comments.quote_zh: 我喜欢 Jonathan Blow 对这种模式的叫法：“Big Agenda language”。
comments.text_zh: 编辑：我已经删掉了关于我认为这门语言有多好用的部分，因为那跑题了。我不确定它是不是最不过度设计的语言。你这么说就像在说 C 很简单，因为只有内存和函数！或者，借用 [LINK] 里的例子：Python：如果一切都是 dict 呢？Java：如果一切都是对象呢？JavaScript：如果一切都是 dict *而且*是对象呢？C：如果一切都是指针呢？APL：如果一切都是数组呢？Tcl：如果一切都是字符串呢？Prolog：如果一切都是 term 呢？LISP：如果一切都是 pair 呢？Scheme：如果一切都是函数呢？Haskell：如果一切都是 monad 呢？汇编：如果一切都是寄存器呢？但不管怎样，通常都有非常非常多的细节（Haskell 也不例外），而且这些细节很重要。另外，想做出任何有质量的东西都需要大量经验！我喜欢 Jonathan Blow 对这种模式的叫法：“Big Agenda language”。如果一门语言如此有主见，可能会让程序员的日子更难过。（从这里开始看：[VIDEO]）他特别点名 Haskell、Java 和其他几个，说它们犯了这种毛病，而且因为坚持意识形态上的纯粹而变得不太好用。
comments.text: EDIT: I have removed what I said about what I think how usable the language is, because it's off-topic. I'm not sure it's the least over-engineered language. What you say is like saying that C is simple because there is only memory and functions! Or, to take from for example [LINK] Python: What if everything was a dict? Java: What if everything was an object? JavaScript: What if everything was a dict *and* an object? C: What if everything was a pointer? APL: What if everything was an array? Tcl: What if everything was a string? Prolog: What if everything was a term? LISP: What if everything was a pair? Scheme: What if everything was a function? Haskell: What if everything was a monad? Assembly: What if everything was a register? But in any case, there are typically lots and lots of details (Haskell is no exception), and they matter. And also, it takes a lot of experience to get anything of quality done! I like what Jonathan Blow calls this pattern: "Big Agenda language". It might make a programmer's life harder if the language is so opinionated. (Start here: [VIDEO] ) He specifically named Haskell, Java, and a few others, as being guilty of that, and being less usable for sticking to ideological purity.

comments.story_title: A Programming Language for Games: Demo [video]
comments.quote_zh: 这艘船已经带我们走了很远，但现在它的航行结束了
comments.text_zh: 他对于 C++ 的感受，在他的第一段视频[0]里被突出表达为“这艘船已经带我们走了很远，但现在它的航行结束了”，这几乎和我想象中 C++ 在未来几年会如何发展完全相反。毫无疑问，C++17 将是一个成败攸关的规范，决定它是否会被其他语言超越；但凭借其庞大的既有地位，以及如今工具和编译器的推进速度（感谢 Clang），我就是看不到近期有任何东西能超过它。C++11/14 确实感觉像是一门不同于 '03 的语言，而我个人毫不怀疑 C++17 又会带来更好的感觉。令人有希望的是，目前投入这门语言的大部分工作，都是要在改善开发者体验和降低复杂性方面取得重大进展。Jonathon 在这么短时间里为自己的语言投入的工作非常令人印象深刻，想法及其实现看起来也很扎实，但我认为他真的低估了把这样的东西从开创阶段推进到生产阶段所需的时间……记住，C++ 在 1983 年还是编译到 C 的。即便在今天，也有其他有意思的语言在走这条路。Vala 和 Nimrod 都浮现在脑海中。在第三段视频结尾，他谈到现代的开创精神与太空竞赛鼎盛时期的那种精神……好吧，50 年后的今天，事实证明太空旅行仍然很难。我不认为编程有什么不同。[0] [VIDEO]
comments.text: The way he feels about C++, highlighted in his first video[0], "this ship has taken us pretty far, but now it's done sailing", is pretty much the opposite of how I feel C++ is going to play out in the next few years. C++17 will no doubt be a make-or-break specification with regard to being surpassed by other languages, but with its critical mass of incumbency, and the rate at which tools and compilers are moving now (thanks Clang), I just don't see anything topping it in the near future. C++11/14 does feel like a different language to '03, and I've personally got no doubt that C++17 will feel better again. Promisingly, almost all of the work going in to the language atm is about making major strides in improving developer experience and reducing complexity. The work Jonathon has put in to his language in such a short time is super-impressive, and the ideas and their implementation seems solid, but I think he's really underestimating the time frames required to get something like this up from the pioneering stage to production ... remember that C++ was compiling to C in 1983 . There are other interesting languages taking this approach even today. Vala and Nimrod both spring to mind. At the end of this third video he talks about modern pioneering spririt versus those from the heyday of the space race... well here we are 50 years later, and it turns out that space travel is still hard. I don't think programming is any different. [0] [VIDEO]
